source.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Emotion Control in Text-to-Speech
source.authors: Hong-Fei Du; Jia-Cheng Shi; Sidi Lu; Gang Zhou; Ye Gao

record.tranche_reason: The study compares SAE dictionary dimensions and reports how feature organization changes, but it does not measure parent-child feature correspondence, input partitioning, or direction similarity.
record.gate_note: The Appendix B dimension-sensitivity result bears on dictionary-size effects. The emotion-steering, acoustic, and cross-backbone results do not measure feature splitting as defined in the claim and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses a Top-k SAE as a tool for emotion steering in IndexTTS2 and mainly reports its steering method's performance. The only bearing on dictionary size is one qualitative sentence in Appendix B. It justifies choosing the 4,096-latent SAE and reports no measurement of feature correspondence, input coverage, decoder-direction similarity or hierarchy. That is not enough to count as a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right for Appendix B: the 10,240-latent SAE lowered reconstruction error but fragmented emotion features, so the authors kept 4,096 latents. The paper's main conclusion, however, is that emotion is distributed across a few sparse SAE latents in the TTS semantic backbone, and that steering a selectivity-ranked top-6 set gives bidirectional emotion control. That control is comparable or superior to global steering and TTS baselines.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Top-k SAE trained on IndexTTS2 semantic-backbone activations and compares latent dimensions; it does not perform the feature matching or input-coverage analysis specified by the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE latent dimension: the 10,240-dimensional model had more fragmented features and lower emotional interpretability than the 4,096-dimensional model.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The size-sensitivity result is qualitative; no feature correspondence, input-overlap, or decoder-direction similarity is reported for the two dimensions.
record.rows_left_out: Main emotion-steering, acoustic, and cross-backbone results were omitted because they do not measure feature splitting across SAE sizes.

untested.parts: Whether larger-SAE features replace a coarse feature, cover its inputs, or lie near its direction; only a qualitative fragmentation remark is given.
Large-LM or open SAE releases; only a speech TTS backbone is studied, and the LLaSA analysis is steering only.
No nested families or concept hierarchy are analysed.
No parent/child firing or absorption analysis is done.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, and no novel-latent analysis.

record.verdict_notes: Downgraded from the reader's tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The dictionary-size remark is anecdotal, with no numbers beyond the two sizes. It is qualitatively consistent with V1, but it cannot ground a verdict. The reader's limits_scope label on V1 is removed.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not show whether a coarse feature is replaced by features that cover the same inputs, whether their decoder directions are nearby, or whether individual features can be matched across dictionary sizes.
The cross-backbone analysis measures emotion alignment under steering, not dictionary-size splitting or open SAE releases.
No nested feature families or concept hierarchy are measured.
The study does not test parent-child activation coverage or whether size or sparsity changes resolve absorption.
The study does not decompose larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents or assess novel latents or canonical units.
The study does not compare training objectives or test whether splitting is an artifact of the sparsity objective.

rows.subject: IndexTTS2
rows.size_stated: SAE dictionary dimensions: 4,096 and 10,240 latent features
rows.stage_stated: Layer-16 pre-LayerNorm residual stream during semantic-token generation
rows.operation_detail: Trained and compared SAEs with different latent dimensions.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of emotion-related features and interpretability
rows.value: For the 10,240-dimensional SAE, emotion-related features became more fragmented and distributed across a larger number of sparse directions, reducing emotional interpretability.
rows.note: The result reports fragmentation with increased dictionary dimension, but does not establish that the larger features partition a smaller feature's inputs or lie near its direction.
rows.check: This is a one-sentence, unquantified remark used to justify a hyperparameter choice, so it is effectively a selection rationale rather than a measured result. 'More fragmented' emotion features at 10,240 latents is qualitatively in the direction of V1. But no coarse-to-fine matching, input coverage or direction similarity is reported, so V1's effect cannot be read off it. The reader's 'partial' state is unsupported. The lower interpretability it reports is not something V1 denies, so it does not limit V1's scope.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The larger dictionary produced more fragmented emotion-related features and reduced interpretability, but the study does not establish coherent splits with shared input coverage or nearby directions (r1).
